 Where Michigan gubernatorial candidates stand on SNAP benefits and its future
 John James, Jocelyn Benson debate over use of SNAP benefits
 Samantha Sayles , Senior Digital Producer
 Published:  October 21, 2026 at 5:00 AM Tags:  Decision 2026 , Politics , Michigan Michigan gubernatorial candidates John James and Jocelyn Benson were asked during a debate how they would manage SNAP benefits in the state.
 One in eight Michiganders live in poverty. As of Oct. 1, Michigan pays 75% of the cost of running SNAP, up from 50%. The state will also have to pay more for benefits. The candidates were asked what they would do for families who depend on SNAP if federal food assistance shrinks.
 James said SNAP needs to be protected for those it was meant for, and he would issue waivers to protect people in high-unemployment areas and where people need it most.
 “These are benefits that should not go to able-bodied adults without dependents who are choosing not to work, and it certainly should not go to illegals,” James said. “We need to get rid of the fraud in our system.”
 Benson said food grown in Michigan can help reduce the state’s food costs. She said she’s been working with farmers to ensure that food is grown in the state.
 “So I’ve got a plan to ensure food is affordable, while we’re also not cutting necessary SNAP benefits that support so many families,” Benson said.
 You can listen to the candidate’s full statements from the Oct. 15 debate on SNAP benefits in Michigan by watching the video at the top of this article.
